Pradeep Kumar Srivastava

For the Appellant : Mr. S.P. Roy, Advocate For the State : APP For the Respondent-2 : Mr. S. S. Choudhary, Advocate For the Victim : Mr. Aashish Kr. Thakur,
Advocate ---
Order No. 05 Dated 02nd December, 2025 I.A. No. 10843 of 2025 Heard the learned counsel for the respective parties.
This application has been preferred by the appellant for grant of bail to him during the pendency of this appeal.

The appellant has been convicted for the offences u/s 366/ 376(2)(n) of the IPC and Section 6 of the POCSO Act and has been sentenced to undergo R.I. for 20 years along with a fine of Rs. 20,000/-
for the offence u/s 6 of the POCSO Act.
It has been alleged that the appellant has enticed away the daughter of the informant.
Submission has been advanced by the learned counsel for the appellant that the victim has solemnized marriage with the appellant and is residing at her matrimonial house for the last one year.
Learned counsel appearing for the respondent No. 2 as well as the learned counsel appearing for the victim have accepted the said fact.
In fact the victim has appeared before us along with her mother-in- law and grandfather-in-law and has accepted the fact that she is residing at her matrimonial house for more than one year.

sentences.text: On consideration of the aforesaid development, we are inclined to admit the appellant on bail.

Accordingly, during pendency of this appeal, the appellant is directed to be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 10,000/- (Rs. Ten Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned trial court [Special Judge (POCSO), Godda] in connection with Special (POCSO) Case No. 10 of 2024.
This I.A. stands allowed and disposed of.
